chunks: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Abu Basir, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Whoever guarantees the death of Abdullah to me, I will guarantee the Qa'im to him.' Then he said: 'When Abdullah dies, the people will not agree upon anyone after him, and this matter will not end except with your Master, if Allah wills. The dominion of years will pass away and the dominion of months and days will begin.' I asked: 'Will that be prolonged?' He replied: 'No.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to political leadership and the duration of rule after the death of the Imam according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the transition from the stable, long-lasting rule of the Imams to a period of fragmented, short-lived political authority following the death of 'Abd Allah (widely identified by Shia scholars as Imam al-Mahdi ibn al-Hasan). The Prophet’s successor, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), clarifies that this era of rapid succession and instability will be brief, serving as a prelude to the reappearance of the Qa'im, thereby emphasizing the transient nature of worldly power compared to the eternal authority of the Imam.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 445 - It is narrated from Fadhl from Uthman bin Isa from Darast Abi Mansur from Ammar bin Marwan from Abu Basir that he said:

I heard Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) say: “I am prepared to guarantee Imam Qaim to one who guarantees the death of Abdullah; because after the death of Abdullah, the Muslims will not have consensus on any one person and this matter will not end, except with your Imam. If Allah wills, the kingdom running into years will end and the kingdom running into days and months will begin.” I (the narrator) asked: “Would this matter be prolonged?” He replied: “Definitely not.”
